headline: High-risk cloud-workspace coder paired with local-only document processor creates dangerous write, injection, and compliance pathways by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, Slack, GitHub, Jira, Notion, and MCP outputs in a cloud workspace, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction-following loop. Pathway has no input surfaces or execution, so it is not itself an injector, but the pair still has a plausible bridge if Devin consumes Pathway-produced documents or artifacts as trusted content.
conditions: IF Devin reads Pathway-generated documents or tickets as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF a shared integration or workspace is added between the agents, attacker-controlled text can bridge into Devin.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from imported documents.
Require provenance labels on Pathway outputs before Devin reads them.
Route Pathway outputs through a human review step.
Restrict Devin MCP servers to allowlisted, signed sources.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace with broad network egress and write-capable integrations. Pathway is local-only in the profile, but if it processes or forwards Devin-originated files, sensitive data can be duplicated into another work product. The pair lacks direct evidence of shared storage, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Devin processes secrets or private repo content and Pathway receives those files, leakage into additional outputs occurs.
IF Pathway is connected to any shared workspace or export path, copied data may persist outside Devin's workspace.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from files sent to Pathway.
Use a redaction step before any handoff.
Keep Pathway on a separate workspace with no shared mounts.
Audit exports for sensitive fields before release.
requires-engineering: implement DLP on the handoff boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad write, shell, git, and network capabilities, while Pathway has none of those capabilities in the profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible overlap is indirect through shared integrations or files, so the pair is lower risk than a same-directory multi-writer setup.
conditions: IF Pathway is given write access to the same repo or workspace as Devin, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared mutable state, concurrent edits can collide.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only relative to Devin's workspace.
Avoid shared git branches for automated writes.
Serialize any handoff through a single owner process.
Use file-level locks for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act on outputs via GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion, so if Pathway-produced text is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or tickets. Pathway is a document-processing agent with no verification or action authority, so the main risk is Devin trusting its output too much.
conditions: IF Devin consumes Pathway output without a verification step, incorrect facts can propagate downstream.
IF Devin is allowed to create tickets or commits from Pathway summaries, the error blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require a second-pass verifier before Devin acts.
Mark Pathway output as untrusted by default.
Limit Devin to draft-only actions for Pathway-derived tasks.
Add citation checks on generated summaries.
requires-engineering: enforce policy gates before external writes.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace handling source code, team chat, and integration tokens, while Pathway is open-source and appears local-only with no declared compliance controls. The pair creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch for code or chat data, but there is no direct evidence of PHI or regulated data, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or region-bound data is routed through Devin and then into Pathway, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
IF the deployment requires documented certifications for both agents, Pathway's unverified status becomes a compliance gap.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention and deletion behavior for both tools.
Restrict Devin to non-sensitive repositories.
Review vendor DPAs and hosting regions.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations.
